newsitem.title: USA: Suspect in Pan Am 103 bombing says he innocent.
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Pan Am 103 bombing says he innocent.

text.p: A Libyan indicted in the United States and Britain for the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am jet that exploded over Lockerbie, Scotland, said he was willing to stand trial in a neutral country, the CBS programme "60 Minutes" reported on Wednesday.

Abdel Basset Ali al-Megrahi, an alleged Libyan intelligence operative, gave a statement to "60 Minutes" in which he proclaimed his innocence and offered to stand trial in a neutral country, possibly before the World Court in The Hague.
The statement will be broadcast Sunday as part of a report on "60 Minutes" on the mid-air bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 that killed 270 people in the air and on the ground.
In it, he says, "As once President Clinton imagined, don't jump to the conclusion -- maybe you could be wrong."
Al-Meghrahi and another suspect, Al-Amin Khalifa Fhimah, both of whom are in Libya, have been indicted in Britain and the United States on charges of placing the bomb aboard the Pan Am flight.
Those countries demand they stand trial in a Scottish or U.S. court.

London and Washington have repeatedly rejected offers by Libya, backed by the Arab League, the Organisation of African Unity and the non-aligned movement, for them to be tried by a Scottish judge under Scottish law but at the World Court at The Hague.
Libya says they could not get a fair trial in Britain or the United States.
